# Your first weeks

Starting in a new lab involves learning the research, the people, and the practical routines. Use this page as a checklist and adapt it to your role; it is not a substitute for formal safety, ethics, or employment instructions.

## Meet the people

Arrange an introduction with your supervisor and immediate collaborators. Find out who can help with day-to-day questions about equipment, participant scheduling, data, computing, and administration. Add a current team directory or link here once the lab agrees where it should live.

## Get set up

Confirm the following with your supervisor or the designated administrator:

- institutional account, email, calendar, and relevant mailing lists;
- building access and any required safety or facility training;
- approved storage and backup locations for research data;
- access to lab software, equipment, and shared resources;
- where protocols, templates, and current project documentation are kept.

Do not move research data to personal cloud storage or devices unless the institution's rules explicitly allow it.

## Learn how the lab works

Ask your supervisor about meeting cadence, progress updates, feedback, authorship expectations, and how to raise a concern. Read the [meeting guidance](../lab-basics/meetings.qmd) and [communication guidance](../lab-basics/people-and-communication.qmd).

## Make a first-month plan

Agree on a short plan with your supervisor: what to read, which people to meet, any training to complete, and one manageable first task. Record relevant deadlines and review the plan together after a few weeks.
